messages.author: d3a6e99cf9fdd5f7
messages.subject: Plotting specific random effects
parts:
Is there anyway to plot just one set of random effects (excluding the second set). For instance:

   f(pollutant.cluster, model="iid") + f(census_tract, model="iid")

All I want to do is plot the pollutant clusters, but can't seem to isolate that one portion of the model using the plot() command. And INLA won't plot anything because the "census_tract" variable is too large.

Thanks,
Eric

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Plotting specific random effects
parts:
On Sat, 2015-04-04 at 08:48 -0700, Eric Coker wrote:
> Is there anyway to plot just one set of random effects (excluding the
> second set). For instance:
>
> f(pollutant.cluster, model="iid") + f(census_tract, model="iid")
>
> All I want to do is plot the pollutant clusters, but can't seem to
> isolate that one portion of the model using the plot() command. And
> INLA won't plot anything because the "census_tract" variable is too
> large.
>

Hi,

you have access to the raw results, either as summaries
(mean,median,quantiles,sd,,...) using

result$summary.random$pollutant.cluster

or the posterior marginals densities itself, as

result$marginals.random$pollutant.cluter

(which is a list if lists...)

hence, you can easily plot it yourself.

H


--
Håvard Rue

you can also add


+ f(e,nsus_tract, model="iid", compute=FALSE)


saying that these marginals are not computed, hence not plotted. with
this, then plot(result) should be ok.
